title: VicCA Simulation and Correlation Function Computation
action: Implement the Vicinal Cellular Automaton (VicCA) model according to the described square-lattice, periodic/helical boundary conditions, CA incorporation rules (unconditional kink/void filling, critical nucleus size 2 at steps, 4 on terraces), fixed potential well depth E_V = 1 k_BT, adatom concentration c0 = 0.01, and independent diffusion attempts n_DS and Ehrlich-Schwoebel barrier E_ES. Run simulations on both flat and vicinal (initial terrace width l0=10) surfaces for the parameter sweeps needed: for scaling exponents, n_DS in {1,2,5,10,15,20} with E_ES=3 k_BT, recording surface height at multiple time points up to 10^6 steps; for the morphology diagram, the grid n_DS ∈ {1,2,5,10,15,20} × E_ES ∈ {0.0,1.0,2.0,2.2,2.4,2.5,2.6,2.8,3.0,4.0,5.0,6.0,7.0,8.0} k_BT, recording final height maps. For each relevant snapshot compute the directional height-height correlation functions C_x(x) and C_y(y) (average squared height difference along the two directions) and extract the first minimum (wavelength λ) and first maximum (amplitude A) for both directions. Save intermediate data (height maps or correlation results) so that subsequent steps can recover the wavelength and amplitude time series.
description: Generates all raw surface height maps and correlation function time series required to derive the scored scaling exponents and morphology diagram.

title: Extract Time-Scaling Exponents
action: Using the wavelength (λ) and amplitude (A) time series from step 1, fit the scaling laws λ ∼ t^{1/z} and A ∼ t^β in the monotonic growth regimes. Compute the dynamic exponent 1/z and growth exponent β along the x (across steps) and y (along steps) directions for each n_DS ∈ {1,2,5,10,15,20} on both flat and vicinal surfaces. For flat surfaces the x and y values are identical; duplicate the value in both columns. Write the results to scaling_exponents.csv.
description: Fitted time-scaling exponents (dynamic and growth) for six n_DS values on flat and vicinal surfaces.
output_schema: CSV with columns: n_DS (int), surface_type (str, 'flat' or 'vicinal'), exponent_1z_x (float), exponent_1z_y (float), exponent_beta_x (float), exponent_beta_y (float). Rows for n_DS = 1,2,5,10,15,20 on both surfaces. For flat surfaces, exponent_1z_x = exponent_1z_y and exponent_beta_x = exponent_beta_y.

title: Classify Morphologies and Produce ES Barrier Diagram
action: For each (n_DS, E_ES) combination in the grid n_DS ∈ {1,2,5,10,15,20} × E_ES ∈ {0.0,1.0,2.0,2.2,2.4,2.5,2.6,2.8,3.0,4.0,5.0,6.0,7.0,8.0} k_BT, use the final-time correlation function data (wavelengths and amplitudes) from step 1 to classify the surface morphology as 'meander', 'mound', or 'mixed' based on anisotropy criteria. Write the classification to morphology_diagram_es.csv.
description: Morphology classification for the (n_DS, E_ES) grid reproducing the principal ES barrier diagram.
output_schema: CSV with columns: n_DS (int), E_ES (float, in units of k_BT), morphology (str, one of 'meander', 'mound', 'mixed'). Covers the specified grid of 6 n_DS × 14 E_ES values. Each cell has a single classification.
